question: According to Gell and Coombs classification, IGE antibodies play role in which hypersensitivity reaction?
explanation: The Gell and Coombs classification categorizes hypersensitivity reactions into four types based on immune mechanisms: 1. Type I (Immediate): IgE-mediated; involves mast cells and basophils (e.g., anaphylaxis, allergies). 2. Type II (Cytotoxic): IgG/IgM- mediated; targets cell surfaces or ECM (e.g., hemolytic anemia, Goodpasture's syndrome). 3. Type III (Immune Complex): Deposition of antigen-antibody complexes; leads to inflammation (e.g., lupus, serum sickness). 4. Type IV (Delayed): T-cell mediated; involves macrophages and cytokines (e.g., contact dermatitis, TB).
